newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC says to cut 445 jobs at Kambalda.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC says to cut 445 jobs at Kambalda.

text.p: WMC Ltd said on Tuesday it would cut 445 jobs from its Kambalda nickel and gold operations in Western Australia.
The cuts followed a review of the Kambalda operations by the company and were designed to improve the operation's efficiency, a WMC spokesman said.
The spokesman said 387 jobs would be cut immediately, with the balance going over the next several months.

The spokesman said the lost jobs represented about half the Kambalda workforce. In a subsequent statement, WMC said specialist mining contractors would be used to operate the remainder of the underground operations at Kambalda in order to cut costs and secure the long-term operation of the complex.

"The decision follows an extensive review which critically assessed the options available to the company in light of relatively high costs, limited operational flexibility, and an increasingly competitive international and national marketplace," the company said.
WMC said it was committed to development in the Kambalda area, noting that it was spending A$30 million to upgrade a nickel concentrator and would spend a further A$24 million on exploration.
Kambalda produced 37,460 tonnes of nickel contained in concentrate in the 1995/96 year ended June 30, company figures show.
The company said it expected that the majority of the workers would be employed by the outside contractors.
Mining contractor firms Brynecut Mining, Eltin Ltd, Henry Walker Group Ltd and GBF have been awarded contracts to operate seven mines in Kambalda, WMC said.
The mines are Long-Victor, Otter-Juan, Coronet, Lanfranchi, Britannia-Sirius and Revenge, the company said.
In Kambalda, WMC already operates three underground nickel mines, two underground gold mines and all its open cut gold oeprations under contract mining arrangements, the company noted.
